title: Gildas: Anchovy, Olive and Guindilla Skewers
summary: Basque-style skewers of anchovy wrapped around a green olive and topped with pickled guindilla peppers, finished with a drizzle of good olive oil.
equipment: 24 short cocktail skewers or toothpicks (10 cm)

ingredients.item: anchovy fillets in olive oil, drained
pickled guindilla peppers, cut in half crosswise

steps.title: Dry
steps.text: Spread the anchovies and peppers on paper towels and pat them dry. Without the surface oil and brine, the pieces grip the skewer and the final drizzle of olive oil clings instead of sliding off.

steps.title: Wrap
steps.text: Curl one anchovy fillet around the middle of each olive. Soft fillets bend easily, so handle them gently to avoid tearing.

steps.title: Skewer
steps.text: Push a skewer through the anchovy and olive so the wrap is held closed, then thread on 2 pepper halves and curve them over the top of the olive. The skewer keeps everything in place for a single bite.

steps.title: Dress
steps.text: Line the gildas up on a platter and drizzle them with the olive oil just before serving. Fresh oil softens the saltiness and gives them a glossy finish.

tips: Overloading is the usual mistake: a gilda is one bite, so stick to one olive, one anchovy and two pepper halves.
Buy good anchovies in olive oil; they are meatier and less harsh than very cheap ones.
No guindillas? Use mild pickled green chillies, sliced into strips.
Serve with plain bread, since they are salty.
storage: Assembled gildas keep covered in the fridge for up to 2 hours; add the oil just before serving. Store any leftover ingredients in their jars in the fridge. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
